newsitem.title: USA: US Gulf spot natgas edges up with short-term heat.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf spot natgas edges up with short-term heat.

text.p: U.S. Gulf spot natgas prices moved slightly higher Thursday as a temporary heat spell in the central U.S. and Northeast triggered more buying interest, industry sources said.

Swing prices on the Gulf Coast pipes began this morning's trading on a soft note but quickly rebounded to land about one to two cents higher than Wednesday's levels in the $1.65-1.70 per million British thermal units range.
On Transco (Station 65) prices held fairly steady in the low-$1.70s, while at the Henry Hub, La., gas traded as high as $1.75.
Despite today's slight uptick in the Gulf markets, forecasters are calling for much cooler temperatures to arrive throughout most of the U.S., excluding the Northwest, this Sunday and Monday.
Some of this downward pressure was felt in the New York city-gate market today where prices slipped into the low-$2 to high-$1.90s area, down five to 10 cents from Wednesday.
Prices were similarly softer in the Appalachian region as traders reported closing most swing deals in the low-to-mid $1.80s.
Some reluctance on the part of buyers was also seen in the West Texas markets. Deals were confirmed done in the Permian basin in the high-$1.40s to about $1.50, down more than five cents on the day.
The margin between Permian and Waha widened again to about nine or 10 cents as gas sold at the western hub in the high-$1.50s. On Transwestern, gas sold mostly in the high-$1.40s.
At the southern California border, prices tailed off into the high-$1.50s to low-$1.60s, indicating a day's loss of about five cents.
In the Midcontinent, trading was fairly active but prices barely budged from the mid-$1.50s. Traders attributed the stability to moderating temperatures expected in the region late this weekend.
